derived_from.note: Same defect, re-grounded on a path the LIVE body can actually reach. The fork execution's own shape does NOT reproduce here: on the fork the superseded token is re-attached after the pick by block (C) ('a customer pick narrows WHO, not WHAT'), which live does not have, and live's coarser order-domain axis map (product and customer both on order_scope) makes the entity-op executor evict it. The live-reachable route is applyDymPick's PREPEND arm - dym_replace_unmatched.

source.rationale: P22 / captain plan A4. Exec 13688567 (fork 13688574): the bot asked "Couldn't find WESRP10B. Did you mean WESERP10B?", the customer answered with the exact code offered, and got the identical question back - for as long as they cared to keep answering, because the superseded spelling stayed a live filter, kept resolving to nothing, and kept re-triggering its own did-you-mean. Here the offer records for_raw as the customer originally spaced it ('WESRP 10B') while the entity in state carries the hyphenated form, so applyDymPick's for_raw tier misses, for_canonical is null, and the for_hint tier sees TWO products - ambiguous - so the pick is PREPENDED and the dead spelling survives alongside it (dym_replace_unmatched). That spacing gap is exactly why the A4 block compares on alphanumerics only. No words are matched: dym_pick_applied says the turn accepts a correction, dym_offer.candidates[].for_raw says which token that candidate was for, and WESRP-10B is retired only because the customer named the code that supersedes it. ABC-1, which no candidate corrects, is untouched.
